title: Protect multilevel gridded data
text: Protection multilevel gridded data using quadtree approach. gridy builds variable-resolution grids geolocated data. idea overlay several nested square grids, coarsest finest, decide cell whether can disseminated merged neighbours order meet confidentiality threshold. result grid whose resolution adapts density: fine wherever counts allow , coarse elsewhere. method developed Insee explained paper presented conference (Journées de Méthodologie Statistique) 2018. paper (French) available . method presented NTTS 2023 conference, poster downloadable .

title: Protect multilevel gridded data
text: package ships C++ code (Rcpp). Installing source requires working toolchain: Rtools Windows, r-base-dev Debian/Ubuntu. Dependencies: data.table, Rcpp, rlang, purrr, sf, fasterize, raster.

title: Protect multilevel gridded data
text: Cells form tree. cell level (parent) subdivided cells level +1 (children). Level 1 coarsest resolution, last level finest. algorithm walks tree one level time. parent cell, examines children increasing order count assigns three attributes: parent cell disseminated passes state entire descent: whole branch stays aggregated. parent cell can disseminated lets children assessed individually, smallest ones absorbed group threshold reached. Cell identifiers follow Inspire specification: FR_CRS3035RES1000mN2000000E3000000, stated position lower left corner.

title: Protect multilevel gridded data
code: library(gridy) library(data.table)  # Geolocated individual data: x, y and the coordinate reference system n <- 1e4 tab <- as.data.table(   data.frame(     id_obs = 1:n,     x = rnorm(n, 3e6, 2e4),     y = rnorm(n, 2e6, 3e4),     crs = 3035   ) )  # 1. Build the variable-resolution grid #    mesh sizes in DECREASING order, threshold of 5 observations tab_GS <- create_GS_CPP(tab, seuil = 5, mailles = c(32e3, 16e3, 8e3, 4e3, 2e3, 1e3))  # 2. Extract the "natural" grid: on each branch of the tree, #    the finest cell that can be disseminated tab_car_nat <- determiner_car_naturel(tab_GS)  # 3. Lookup table between natural cells and finest-level cells arb_nat <- determiner_arb_naturel(tab_car_nat, tab_GS)  # 4. Estimate sensitive variables on protected cells, by distributing #    the group total in proportion to a non-sensitive variable tab_car <- tab_GS$tab_car tab_car[, `:=`(poph = nb_obs * 0.48, popf = nb_obs * 0.52)] tab_diff <- imputer_cle_repartition(   tab_car,   list_var_imput = c("poph", "popf"),   var_cle = "nb_obs" )  # 5. Turn cells into geometries for mapping contours <- lapply(tab_car_nat$id_carreau_nat, make_contour_car)

text: Mesh order validated. create_GS_CPP() assumes mailles sorted decreasing order: mailles[1] becomes level 1, last element finest grid. increasing vector yields inconsistent tree without raising error. differs create_grids(), sorts input . Mesh sizes must nested. mesh size multiple next one (32-16-8-4-2-1 km works).
